extracted.intended_audience: observatory astronomers and positional astronomers preparing or using meridian/mural/repeating-circle observations (e.g., observatory staff, data reducers, historical astronomy researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and reporting standards for meridian/mural/repeating-circle solar, planetary, and stellar observations and their reductions (solstices, conjunctions, oppositions, comet positions). Covers what to record, which corrections to apply, averaging methods, epoch reductions, and how omitted corrections are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record observation mode (direct or by reflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the observation was made direct or by reflection (e.g., 'Observed alternately direct and by reflection').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mark for each solstice/observation if it was observed direct, by reflection, or alternately; used in reductions and in assessing systematic differences between modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record limb used (upper, lower, centre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate which limb of the Sun or planet was observed (upper limb, lower limb, or centre) in the entry ('Limb. U / L / centre').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different limbs require distinct semidiameter and limb-specific corrections; report limb per observation and compute limb-specific means (mean by upper limbs, mean by lower limbs, mean of centre).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record instrumental and environmental readings (barometer, thermometer, microscopes, semidiameter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include barometer, thermometer, semidiameter, and microscope readings for each observation (columns labelled 'Barom.', 'Therm.', 'Microscopes.', 'Semidiameter').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metadata are required to compute corrections (refraction, temperature/pressure-dependent effects) and to evaluate instrument performance (e.g., mean of the four microscopes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply refraction corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct observed zenith/ polar distances for atmospheric refraction ('Refract.' column; 'Mer. Zen. Dist. ... corrected for Refraction').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the refraction constants or method used (e.g., 'Bessel’s Refract.' appears in tables). Document when refraction has been applied and which formula/constants were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply parallax corrections when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply parallax corrections to planetary/solar observations where required ('Parallax' or 'Par.' column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parallax is not applied, explicitly state this (examples: 'The following South Polar Distances of Venus ... are neither corrected for refraction nor parallax.'; 'N.B. Parallax has not been applied.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply semidiameter correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and apply semidiameter corrections for the observed body (column 'Semidiameter' / 'Semidiam.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semidiameter corrections depend on limb observed (upper/lower) and must be accounted for in deriving centre positions or polar distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct for Sun’s latitude (Sun’s Lat.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply correction for the Sun's latitude where required (column 'Corr. for Sun’s Lat.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This correction is included in the reduction pipeline for solar observations and must be reported per observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce observations to a common epoch/date (e.g., Solstice or Jan 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce measured quantities to a standard epoch or the solstice date ('Reduction to Solstice', 'Reduction to January 1, 1823', 'Reduction to Jan. 1, 1828').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the target epoch and show reductions (including intermediate corrections). Provide resulting mean values at that epoch (e.g., mean obliquity at Jan 1 X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply luni-solar nutation corrections and note sign/value
rubrics_metrics.description: Include lunisolar nutation correction and its value in the reduction ('Luni-solar nutation . , — 9.8', '+9.3', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the lunisolar nutation applied and its numeric effect; include whether nutation was added or subtracted and the value used when reporting means or reducing to epoch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and apply polar point corrections (from circumpolar stars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a polar point from upper and lower culminations of circumpolar stars and use it to adjust polar distances; or correct polar point by an assumed obliquity for star reductions ('deducing the obliquity of the ecliptic from the polar point found by upper and lower culminations ... as to correct this polar point by an assumed obliquity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether the polar point was applied and whether it was derived independently or corrected by an assumed obliquity. Note special cases where 'P. D. of Tropic not corrected for Polar Point' or 'Polar Point had been previously applied.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute instrument/limb means (mean of four microscopes; mean of upper/lower limbs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report averages such as 'Mean of the four Microscopes' and means separately for upper limbs, lower limbs, and centre ('The mean of all the observations derived from the upper limb ... from the lower limb ... the mean of the two').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these means in final reductions (e.g., to derive obliquity); indicate which averaging procedure was used and prefer documenting separate limb means to detect systematic offsets (e.g., 'this is probably the most correct way to proceed').

rubrics_metrics.name: State omitted corrections explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: When a correction is not applied, explicitly state this in the table or notes (examples: 'not corrected for Polar Point', 'neither corrected for refraction nor parallax', 'Parallax has not been applied').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit omission statements are mandatory so users know which corrections to add when re-reducing data; include N.B. notes where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record interruptions and observational limitations (weather, departures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document interruptions to observing runs (e.g., 'This solstice was interrupted on account of my departure'; 'weather was unfavourable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes about interrupted observations, unfavorable weather, or missing nights should appear alongside the data so that gaps and potential biases are visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduct interval between transits for post-conjunction planetary timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For observations after conjunction: 'the interval between the transits is to be deducted from the sun’s culmination on the next following day, in order to have the transit of Venus on the given day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this timing adjustment when converting subsequent-day culmination times to the true transit time on the given day; document the interval used and the step in the reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify refraction method/constant used (e.g., Bessel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the refraction formulation used in corrections ('Bessel’s Refract.' appears in tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the refraction source/constant is necessary for reproducibility of reductions; include numeric constants where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce planetary observations to the time of planetary culmination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce planetary observations to the Time of the Culmination of the planet (e.g., 'reduced to the Time of the Culmination of Mars').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduction step centers observations on the planet's culmination for consistent RA/Dec/PD reporting; document the time used and any interpolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report positional summaries and relevant orbital/orientation parameters for comets
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting comet positions include mean times, mean RA, mean Declination, and orbital parameters (e.g., 'Logarithm of Perihel. Distance', 'Inclination', 'Motion retrograde').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both positional means and derived orbital information; include the epoch of the orbital elements and any logs used (e.g., log of perihelion distance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record counts and statistical columns (number of observations, differences, mean values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include number of observations, differences (e.g., 'Diff. of Declin.'), means, and other statistics in tables ('No. of Obs.', 'Diff. of Right Asc. in Time', 'Mean Time at Stargard').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and basic statistics to evaluate precision (e.g., scatter among microscopes or repeated transits) and to allow weighting in further analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: State instrument/technique used (mural circle, repeating circle, circular micrometer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate which instrument and technique were used for each set of observations (e.g., 'observed with the Mural Circle', 'with the Repeating Circle', 'Original Observations with a Circular Micrometer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument identity affects applied corrections and uncertainties; report instrument along with reduction steps and any instrument-specific processing (e.g., 'Mean of the four Microscopes' for mural circle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and report assumed obliquity when used for reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assumed obliquity is used to correct polar point or reduce star observations, state its value (example: 'assuming the obliquity = 23° 27' 43.9 as given in the Nautical Almanack').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an assumed obliquity is used rather than a derived one, document the source and value and show effects on derived polar points or reductions.
